title: The Bend and the Hills: Szentendre, Esztergom and the Palóc Villages
subRegion: Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) & the Cserhát Hills, Nógrád County

bestPeriod.window: late April to early June, and the whole of September into mid-October
bestPeriod.avoid: July-August (Szentendre's Fő tér is shoulder-to-shoulder, Danube boats sold out) and January-February (Hollókő shuts down)

transport.note: €90, €150 (small hire car for days 4-7, or rail + ferry throughout)

activities.note: €60, €105 (Skanzen, citadel, basilica cupola, Hollókő castle, museums)

hook: Budapest is forty minutes behind you and it may as well be a different country. This week runs along the Danube where it turns hard south, Serbian church towers in Szentendre, a citadel above Visegrád, Hungary's largest basilica staring across a bridge into Slovakia, then turns inland into the Cserhát, where Hollókő's whitewashed Ófalu has fifty-eight protected houses, an embroidery tradition still worked by hand, and no traffic. Two beds all week. Ferries, slow trains, long lunches.

snapshot.Best period: Late April-early June; September to mid-October
snapshot.Getting there: Budapest Liszt Ferenc (BUD). The **HÉV H5** suburban railway from Batthyány tér reaches Szentendre in about 40 min: a 500 HUF Budapest single plus a suburban supplementary ticket of about 450 HUF for the Békásmegyer-Szentendre section, roughly 950 HUF (~€2.40) each way. A party is better off with MÁV's HÉV *kirándulójegy*, 6,200 HUF for unlimited Békásmegyer-Szentendre travel for up to ten people in a day (2026 tariff). From Day 4, a small hire car picked up in Vác or Budapest makes the Cserhát practical.

itinerary.title: Serbian Szentendre
itinerary.morning: HÉV H5 from Batthyány tér. Drop bags, walk into **Fő tér** and stand at the Merchants' Cross while the day-trippers are still on the train.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Blagovestenska church** on Fő tér itself (1752, an iconostasis behind a plain baroque street front), then up to the Belgrade Cathedral and the Serbian Ecclesiastical Art Collection in the episcopal quarter, the surviving trace of the Serbs who fled north in 1690.
itinerary.evening: Climb Templom tér for the roofs and the river, then dinner in the old town.

itinerary.title: Skanzen and Marzipan
itinerary.morning: Bus or a 4 km ride out to **Skanzen**, the Hungarian Open Air Museum on Sztaravodai út, 300-plus relocated buildings across regional villages, including a full Nógrád street. Allow three hours; the internal narrow-gauge railway is running and saves legs, on its own ticket of 1,400 HUF (1,200 HUF reduced). Admission is 4,000 HUF (~€10) full and 2,000 HUF reduced, rising to 5,000/2,500 HUF on festival days such as Easter, Pentecost and St Martin's; under-6s and over-70s free, and free for under-26s on the second Sunday of the month (2026 tariff).
itinerary.afternoon: Back into town for the **Szabó Marzipan** museum and shop on Dumtsa Jenő utca, then the Margit Kovács ceramic collection, Szentendre's best single art holding.
itinerary.evening: A slow supper on Bogdányi utca; Szentendre empties dramatically after the last HÉV crowd goes home.

itinerary.title: Visegrád by Water
itinerary.morning: Take the **MAHART** boat upriver to Visegrád if the timetable serves, otherwise the H5 to Szentendre station and the bus. The **Royal Palace** of Matthias Corvinus, the Renaissance loggia and the Hercules fountain, sits at river level.
itinerary.afternoon: Up to the **Fellegvár citadel**, 300 m above the river. The bend is the whole point: the Danube swings 90 degrees below you with the Börzsöny on the far bank. Walk or take the shuttle from the Nagyvillám road.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Malomkert Panzió** in Visegrád, then the last boat or bus back to Szentendre.

itinerary.title: Esztergom, and a Bridge into Slovakia
itinerary.morning: Train or car to **Esztergom**. The **Basilica** is the largest church in Hungary, climb the cupola for the Danube and the Slovak hills, and go into the **Bakócz Chapel**, red marble, 1506, dismantled and reassembled stone by stone inside the newer building.
itinerary.afternoon: The Christian Museum in the Primate's Palace, then walk the **Mária Valéria bridge** across to **Štúrovo** in Slovakia, ten minutes, no formalities inside Schengen, and a coffee on the far bank looking back at the dome.
itinerary.evening: Return via **Vác** if the schedule allows: **Március 15. tér**, the 1764 **Triumphal Arch** built by Isidore Canevale for a visit by Maria Theresa, and dinner at **Vén Hajó** on the embankment. Then back to Szentendre and pack.

itinerary.title: Over the Cserhát to Hollókő
itinerary.morning: Collect the car and drive east and north via the M3 and Pásztó. Stop at the **Nógrád** castle ruins on their basalt knoll for twenty minutes and the view over the Cserhát.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in **Hollókő** and walk **Ófalu** end to end, two rows of whitewashed houses with carved timber galleries, the wooden-towered church of 1889 at the fork, and the craft houses: weaving, pottery, embroidery, the doll collection.
itinerary.evening: Settle into **Hollókői Vendégház**. Village dinner, a glass of Nógrád wine, and a street with no cars on it after dark.

itinerary.title: The Castle, and the Palóc Museum
itinerary.morning: Climb to **Hollókő castle** above the village, 13th century, restored, 25 minutes up through oak wood, with the Cserhát ridges laid out in every direction.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to **Szécsény** for the Forgách castle and the **Kubinyi Ferenc Museum**, then on to **Balassagyarmat** for the **Palóc Museum**, costume, embroidery, the reconstructed Palóc house in the garden.
itinerary.evening: Back to Hollókő the slow way through the villages. Eat where you are staying.

itinerary.title: Last Morning in Ófalu, then Budapest
itinerary.morning: Buy embroidery directly from the workshop rather than the gift counter, and one piece of black burnished pottery. If it is Easter weekend, stay for the **Húsvéti Fesztivál**, the Palóc costumes come out and the water-throwing *locsolkodás* is real, not staged; the autumn **wine and harvest weekend** is quieter and better for eating.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive back to Budapest, dropping the car at the airport or in the city.
itinerary.evening: Fly out, or one last dinner in Budapest with the week's embroidery in your bag.

accommodationStrategy.name: A Fő tér-area panzió
accommodationStrategy.description: four nights without repacking, with the HÉV, the MAHART pier and the bus station all within 10 minutes on foot. That combination is what makes the whole Danube leg car-free.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4-6 weeks ahead; longer for the September wine weekend.

accommodationStrategy.name: Malomkert Panzió
accommodationStrategy.description: the alternative Danube base if you prefer the citadel side of the bend to Szentendre's crowds, quieter, greener, its own kitchen, and the Nagymaros ferry five minutes away for the rail connection.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hollókői Vendégház
accommodationStrategy.description: sleeping inside the UNESCO village, not in a hotel below it. Thick whitewashed walls, a timber gallery, and the street to yourself once the coaches leave at five.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6-10 weeks ahead, and much further for Easter weekend, when the village is fully booked months out.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming; 4G/5G along the Danube, thinner in the Cserhát but fine in Hollókő.
logistics.emergency: 112. Hospitals at Vác, Esztergom and Salgótarján; Hollókő has no pharmacy, so stock up in Szécsény.
logistics.weather: the Danube Bend funnels wind and the citadel is 300 m above the river, routinely 5 °C colder and much windier than the bank. Cserhát mornings in October drop close to freezing. Spring Danube high water occasionally closes the Szentendre and Vác embankments and suspends ferry services.
logistics.bookingWindows: Hollókő 6-10 weeks (Easter: months); Szentendre 4-6 weeks; MAHART boats a few days ahead in season, same-day midweek; nothing else requires reservation.
logistics.money: forint, roughly **€1 ≈ 390-405 HUF**. Cards are near-universal, including on MÁV trains and at Skanzen; carry HUF cash for the Hollókő craft houses, the Nagymaros ferry and village markets. Always decline dynamic currency conversion and pay in HUF.
logistics.transportRules: Hungarian motorways require an **e-matrica** vignette, a county sticker is enough if you stay off the M3, but the M3 leg needs a national one; hire cars usually include it, so confirm. Trains on the Szob line are MÁV; buy at the machine or the Vonatinfó app. Bikes travel on the HÉV and on Danube boats for a supplement. Drink-driving limit is zero.
logistics.permits: Ófalu is a living village with residents, photography of house exteriors is fine, of interiors and people only with permission. Drones are prohibited over the Hollókő World Heritage core and over Esztergom Basilica.

proTips: Do Szentendre's Fő tér **before 10:00 or after 18:00**. The HÉV delivers Budapest day-trippers in a wave mid-morning and reclaims them by early evening; the square is a genuinely quiet baroque space on either side of that.

Take the **Nagymaros-Visegrád ferry** rather than driving round via Vác. Five minutes across, costs a couple of euros, and the approach to the citadel from the water is the view the palace was designed for.
At Esztergom, buy the **cupola climb** ticket, not just basilica entry. The nave is free to enter; the dome and the Bakócz Chapel are what you are paying for.
Eat lunch at **Vén Hajó** in Vác on a weekday. Weekend Danube-side tables are booked out by Budapest families by Friday evening.
In Hollókő, the craft houses close around 17:00 with the coaches. Arrange your **embroidery purchase in the afternoon of Day 5** so you are not scrambling on the last morning.
Skanzen's Nógrád section is the same architecture you sleep in three days later. Walk it first, in that order, it turns Hollókő from a pretty street into something you can read.
Useful Hungarian: *"Egy kávét kérek"* and *"a számlát, legyen szíves"*. Tipping is 10%, often already added as *szervizdíj*, check the bill.

raw.Village and town squares by name: **Fő tér**, Szentendre, the triangular baroque square with the 1763 Merchants' Cross, ringed by former Serbian merchant houses. **Március 15. tér**, Vác, the Danube-facing main square with its Dominican church, above which lies the crypt where the 18th-century mummies were found. **Széchenyi tér**, Esztergom, in the Vízivárosi lower town beneath the basilica hill. **Ófalu**, Hollókő, not a square but a single forked street of 58 protected houses on the slope below the castle, UNESCO-listed in 1987 as the surviving example of a pre-agricultural-revolution Palóc village. **Szécsény's** Kubinyi Ferenc square below the Forgách castle and the leaning fire tower.
raw.Market days and artisan specialities: the **Palóc embroidery** of the Nógrád villages, dense red-and-blue floral work on white linen, distinct from Kalocsa's brighter style and still stitched to order in Hollókő and Balassagyarmat. **Palóc pottery**, black-fired and burnished, sold in the Ófalu craft houses. **Szabó Marzipan** in Szentendre, Dumtsa Jenő utca, with its museum room and Hungarian Parliament sculpted in almond paste. Szentendre's produce market off Bükkös part runs strongest on Friday and Saturday mornings; Vác's covered market and Balassagyarmat's weekly market follow the standard Hungarian rhythm of early mornings and Wednesday/Saturday peaks. The **Palóc Museum** in Balassagyarmat, founded 1891, is the reference collection for both traditions.
raw.Boutique and characterful stays: **Malomkert Panzió** in Visegrád, a mill-garden guesthouse with its own restaurant a short walk from the Royal Palace. **Hollókői Vendégház**, village houses inside the protected Ófalu, whitewashed, timber-galleried, some with a *kemence* stove. **Vén Hajó** in Vác, the moored-boat restaurant on the Danube embankment, for a long lunch. **Prima Pékség** for morning pastry and coffee, the reliable small-town bakery counter for a *kakaós csiga* before a train.
raw.Deliberate slow-travel pacing (max one r: **two bases only.** **Szentendre nights 1-4** covers Szentendre itself, Visegrád, Esztergom and Vác by boat, ferry and train, with no packing. **Hollókő nights 5-7** covers Nógrád, Szécsény and Balassagyarmat within a 35 km radius. The single relocation is Szentendre → Hollókő, about 95 km and 1h40 by car via the M3 and the road through Pásztó. Everything on the Danube leg can be done without a car: the **MAHART PassNave** hydrofoil and boat services run Budapest-Szentendre-Visegrád-Esztergom on a seasonal timetable. In 2026 the Budapest-Szentendre-Leányfalu-Visegrád excursion boat ran 22 June to 30 August, Thursday to Sunday, at 7,500 HUF one-way and 9,000 HUF return; the *Bíbic* hydrofoil ran May to September on selected weekends, 11,000 HUF to Visegrád and 13,000 HUF to Esztergom one-way, advance booking only because there is no on-board sale. Treat the timetable as conditional: low water on the Danube suspended or rerouted the Budapest-Szentendre, Budapest-Visegrád and hydrofoil services from 13 July to 13 September 2026, so check mahartpassnave.hu before you build a day around a boat; the Budapest Nyugati, **Szob** line stops at **Nagymaros-Visegrád** and at **Szob**, and the small **Nagymaros-Visegrád ferry** crosses in five minutes, on demand, all year.
